claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I've started the assessment. To help you, I need to ask a few questions about your child or children.

**First, how old is the child (or the oldest child if you have more than one)?**

- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old**
- **20 years old or older**

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm inquiring about my child Alex. He's 6 years old, so under 16.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. So Alex is 6 years old and falls under the 16 category. Let me move forward with the assessment based on this.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(For a 6-year-old, the answer would typically be "yes" - they're not in paid work - but I need to confirm this with you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not working at all. He's only 6, so he's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That makes perfect sense! Alex is in primary school and not working. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, for a 6-year-old in primary school, this would typically be "yes" - they wouldn't be receiving these benefits - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, that's what I expected. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check the apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(For a 6-year-old in primary school, the answer would be "no" - he's not in an apprenticeship. But let me confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not. He's only 6 years old and in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that could make you eligible under the residency requirements:

**Which of the following best describes your situation?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most common situation
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status and are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3+ continuous months)
4. **You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work** (jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** (not claiming Income Support, JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
6. **You have pre-settled status and are studying** (with sufficient resources to support yourself)
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national**
8. **You are a Crown servant living abroad** (or in certain qualifying countries)

Or if none of these apply, please let me know your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask a bit more to understand your situation better.

**You mentioned you're living abroad. Can you tell me:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant?** (e.g., working for the Foreign Office, Ministry of Defence, or similar government roles abroad)

2. **Or are you living in a specific country abroad?** If so, which country?

This will help me determine if you still qualify for Child Benefit under the special circumstances for people living outside the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant. I'm just living abroad with my family - not for government work or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me also check your immigration status to see if any other residency paths might apply:

**Do you have any of the following immigration statuses?**

1. **Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
2. **Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (if so, I'd need to understand your circumstances - whether you're working, studying, jobseeking, or have sufficient resources)
3. **None of the above** - you're simply a UK citizen or have a different immigration status

This will help me determine if there's a route for you to qualify while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any of those statuses. I'm just living abroad currently.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Based on the information you've provided:

- You're living abroad (not in the UK)
- You're not a Crown servant
- You don't have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

Unfortunately, according to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you would not meet the residency requirements. Child Benefit is generally only available to those who normally live in the UK, with some exceptions for Crown servants abroad and those with specific immigration statuses.

Let me navigate to the outcome to confirm this finding:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I have the following outcome for you:

---

## **Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**Explanation:**

Child Benefit is only available to people who normally live in the UK, with limited exceptions. The main exceptions are:
- Crown servants living abroad
- People with settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- People with pre-settled status who meet certain qualifying criteria (working, studying, jobseeking, or having sufficient resources)

Since you are:
- Living abroad
- Not a Crown servant
- Without settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

You do not qualify for Child Benefit at this time, even though Alex (your 6-year-old child) would otherwise be a qualifying child.

**What you might consider:**

- If your situation changes and you move back to the UK, you would become eligible
- If you gain settled status or other qualifying immigration status, you may become eligible
- You may want to contact HMRC directly to discuss your specific circumstances, as there may be other factors not covered in this assessment

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help clarify about your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me. So because I don't live in the UK, I'm not eligible for Child Benefit, even though Alex would otherwise qualify. That's clear now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! Yes, that's exactly right. Alex would be a qualifying child in terms of his age and circumstances, but the residency requirement is a fundamental part of Child Benefit eligibility. Since you're currently living abroad and don't fall into one of the special exception categories, unfortunately you're not able to claim Child Benefit at this time.

If your circumstances change in the future—such as if you move back to the UK—you would then become eligible to claim for Alex.

Let me now record the final outcome of this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect. I've recorded the final assessment. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or if your situation changes in the future, feel free to reach out. Best of luck, and I hope your family enjoys your time abroad!
